Why I read the web in a terminal

By Ada Byron

The terminal has outlived almost every interface that came after it. It is fast, it is scriptable, and it never asks you to wait for a spinner. Reading on the web, by contrast, has become a negotiation with banners, overlays and autoplaying video. The words are in there somewhere.

Reading on the web, by contrast, has become a negotiation with banners, overlays and autoplaying video. The words are in there somewhere. A reader view strips a page down to the text its author wrote, then sets it in a column narrow enough that the eye can find the next line without effort.

The problem with pages

A reader view strips a page down to the text its author wrote, then sets it in a column narrow enough that the eye can find the next line without effort. Typography in a grid of fixed cells is constrained, but the constraints are old friends: bold, italic, underline, and a handful of colours carry a long way.
